name: fool-in-the-rain
description: FAMOUS DRUM SOUND: Led Zeppelin 'Fool In The Rain' / John Bonham. A room-DOMINANT, warm/dark, fat-low-mid, breathing drum bus. The room mic is the loudest layer (the 'reverb'); warmth comes from Helios colour + Studer 15 IPS tape + tilt (NOT bright EQ); glue from the SSL bus comp (the Polar-Studios SSL lineage). This is the TONE, not the half-time shuffle GROOVE, and it NEEDS room mics in the source. Dev-validated 2026-06-03 on a 45 s artifacts/drums clip (a non-Bonham, hyper-dynamic kit). Reproduce the whole pipeline below.
pipeline: 1. SOURCE: phase-aligned multi-mic stems WITH room + overhead mics (drum-prep phase-align -> <kit>/phase-aligned/).

2. PER-STEM PROCESS: scripts/mix/process_stems.py with presets/mix/fool-in-the-rain-stem-process.plans.json (declick OFF; GENTLE corrective clean/de-box/de-harsh — KEEP the low-mid warmth, NO air boosts, no low-mid cuts on the loud room/overhead stems) -> <kit>/processed-fitr/.
3. ROOM-FORWARD BALANCE: scripts/mix/balance_stems.py with the per-role targets below (measured LUFS; ROOM + OVERHEAD the loudest layer, close mics UNDER) -> bus_fitr_pre.wav.
4. BONHAM CHAIN: scripts/mix/fool_in_the_rain_bus.py bus_fitr_pre.wav bus_fitr.wav (Helios colour -> Studer 15 IPS tape -> SSL bus comp -> zero-phase polish; params in that script).

balance_targets_lufs._method: measured integrated LUFS per stem, gained to target; one global -6 dBFS-peak headroom trim on the sum (NOT peak-normalized per stem). THE INVERSION vs warm-tight: room/overhead are FORWARD (loudest), close mics UNDER — the ambience is the sound.

drum room._note: THE STAR — the loudest layer, the 'reverb' (stereo, image preserved)

overhead._note: kit image + cymbals, just under the room (stereo)

snare top._note: deep fat snare; NOT gated so ghost notes survive

hi hat._note: barely — the OH/room carry the cymbals

bus_chain._impl: scripts/mix/fool_in_the_rain_bus.py — authoritative; a bare invocation reproduces these. Helios/Studer/SSL are driven inline via Pedalboard set_param (nearest-valid snap), the same mechanism as the preset harness; apply-vst-chain's float dict would drop the string enums.
1_eq_pre_zero_phase: high_pass 35 Hz q0.707 (keep subsonic out of the tape)

2_helios_type_69._intent: warm British transformer + 700 Hz body colour; NO air (hi_shelf only CUTS up high; bass boost is INERT headless). gain40+pad=-20 dB = the musical ~1.9%-THD-on-a-sine sweet spot; level -14 trims the Mic-gain boost back into the tape.

3_studer_a800_tape._intent: fat ~50-70 Hz head-bump BLOOM + warmth/glue; darkens the top (repro_hf_eq 2). 15 IPS NOT 30 — the bloom IS the Bonham bottom (warm-tight uses 30 to TIGHTEN; do not 'fix' to 30).

4_ssl_bus_compressor_2._intent: clean STEREO VCA glue (preserves the room image, unlike a mono comp). attack 10 ms = classic drum-bus 'breathing' glue. NOTE: a SLOW (30 ms) attack on a peaky drum bus RAISES crest (compresses sustain, not peaks). SC-HPF 60 keeps the kick from pumping the bus.

5_eq_post_zero_phase: bell 300 +1.5 dB q0.8 (200-400 Hz head/low-mid thump)
high_shelf 10000 +0.5 dB q0.7 (GENTLE air, not bright)
bus_chain.6_output: peak-normalize to -1 dBFS (mix bus — NOT mastered)

approved_signature_full_kit._measured_on: a 45 s clip of the artifacts/drums kit (dev smoke test) — a BRIGHT (centroid 4630, tilt -1.5) and HYPER-DYNAMIC (room crest 34) kit, i.e. a stress test, not a Bonham performance.
approved_signature_full_kit._what_to_check: the DIRECTION, not absolutes: centroid DOWN ~1000 Hz (warmer/darker), tilt more negative (warm, ~-2.0 here from -1.5), correlation MODERATE ~0.65-0.85 (the room/OH stereo is preserved — a live room sits well below the warm-tight bus's 0.97). CREST IS CONTENT-DEPENDENT: this kit's room is so dynamic the bus stays ~28; on a more controlled Bonham source expect lower. 'Breathing glue' = a few dB of crest reduction vs the pre-bus, NOT an absolute 16-18.

approved_signature_watercolors_kit._measured_on: the watercolors kit's ROOM-FORWARD pre-bus (projects/watercolors/mix/bus_fitr_pre.wav: centroid 2673 / tilt -1.62 / crest 27.6 / corr 0.833 / LUFS -30.4 — a genuinely wide, hyper-dynamic room). LOCKED 2026-06-04: won the .claude/workflows/fool-in-the-rain.js 5-lens Gemini panel (44/50) over 5 variants, and a SEQUENTIAL re-render reproduced these meters EXACTLY (an independent re-measure agreed: TP -0.99 dBTP). Also surfaced by /famous-drum-shootout as the best-fit character for this kit.
approved_signature_watercolors_kit._judge_panel: /fool-in-the-rain 5-lens panel — winner tight_30ips 44/50: roominess 9, warmth 9, glue 8, lowmid 9, dynamics 9. Runner-ups: no_helios 40 (crest 28.1 — without the Helios colour the room reads 'disconnected/pushed back', -5 on roominess), default_15ips 39 (the recipe default — 30 IPS edged it here), slow_breathe 34 (--ssl-attack 30 raised crest), more_glue 31 (--ssl-thresh -20 over-glued).
approved_signature_watercolors_kit._what_to_check: PER-KIT INVERSION (do NOT change the recipe default): on THIS kit 30 IPS WON over the recipe's standard 15 IPS bloom. The watercolors room is already FAT + hyper-dynamic (pre-bus crest 27.6, tilt -1.62), so 15 IPS over-fattened it while 30 IPS TIGHTENED the low end into the warm/controlled Bonham target (centroid 2673->1896 warm-dark, tilt -1.62->-2.61, crest 27.6->25.5 = breathing not crush, corr 0.833->0.856 = room stereo preserved). 15 IPS remains the documented default for most kits; 30 IPS is the locked setting for THIS kit only. The Helios colour matters (no_helios lost 5 roominess points — the room glue needs it).

notes: Needs ROOM mics — no room channel, no Bonham sound (the room is the loudest layer, the 'reverb').
This is the TONE, not the half-time shuffle GROOVE or the ghost-note performance — those live in the source.
Warmth = Helios colour + Studer 15 IPS tape + tilt, NEVER a bright EQ boost. 15 IPS BLOOMS the lows (fat); do NOT 'fix' it to 30 IPS (that's the warm-TIGHT move).
Keep the low-mid body in the stem-process: gentle de-box only, and NO low-mid cuts in the API color EQ on the loud room/overhead stems (those scoop out the warmth — learned in the dev pass).
Don't slam the SSL — a few dB of glue. A 30 ms attack RAISES crest on peaky drums; 10 ms is the breathing default.

Honest nuance: the real track used an SSL at Polar Studios (Stockholm), NOT a Helios desk. Helios is the repo's era-appropriate Zeppelin-warmth COLOUR; the chase is the tone/feel, not a literal signal path. Run .claude/workflows/fool-in-the-rain.js to A/B Helios-on/off, 15-vs-30 IPS, SSL settings.
This is a MIX bus (peak -1, NOT mastered) — hand to master-track for loudness/limiting and loops-to-deliverables for loops.
